items.q: Find the gradient between (1,2) and (5,10).
Find the gradient between (-2,3) and (4,-9).
Find the gradient of the line y = 3x - 7.
hints: In y = mx + c, the gradient is the coefficient of x.

items.q: Find the gradient between (0,4) and (6,1).
Find the gradient of the line through (2,5) and (10,9).
Find the gradient of y = -4x + 6.
hints: In y = mx + c, the gradient is the coefficient of x.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line 2x + 3y = 12.
hints: Rearrange into y = mx + c form first, then read off the gradient.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 2 through (0,3).
hints: (0,3) is the y-intercept, so c = 3 directly.

items.q: Find the equation of the line through (1,4) with gradient -3.
hints: Substitute the point into y = mx + c to find c.

items.q: Find the equation of the line through (2,5) and (6,13).
hints: Find the gradient first, then substitute one point to find c.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient 4 through (0,-2).
hints: (0,-2) is the y-intercept, so c = -2 directly.

items.q: Find the equation of the line with gradient -1 through (3,5).
hints: Substitute the point into y = mx + c to find c.

items.q: Find the equation of the line through (0,7) and (2,11).
hints: (0,7) is the y-intercept, so c = 7; use the second point to find the gradient.

items.q: Give two points on y = 2x + 1.
hints: Substitute two different x-values into the equation to find matching y-values.

hints: Substitute two different x-values into the equation to find matching y-values.

hints: y = 3 means y is always 3, whatever x is.

hints: Substitute two different x-values into the equation to find matching y-values.

items.q: Give two points on y = -2x + 6.
hints: Substitute two different x-values into the equation to find matching y-values.

items.q: Give two points on x = 4.
hints: x = 4 means x is always 4, whatever y is.

items.q: Find the intersection of y = 2x + 1 and y = 9 - x.
hints: At the intersection, both equations have the same y-value — set them equal.

items.q: Find the intersection of y = 3x - 2 and y = x + 6.
hints: At the intersection, both equations have the same y-value — set them equal.

items.q: Find the intersection of y = -x + 7 and y = 2x + 1.
hints: At the intersection, both equations have the same y-value — set them equal.

items.q: Find the intersection of y = x + 4 and y = 2x + 1.
hints: At the intersection, both equations have the same y-value — set them equal.

items.q: Find the intersection of y = 5 - x and y = x - 1.
hints: At the intersection, both equations have the same y-value — set them equal.

items.q: Find the intersection of y = 4x + 3 and y = x + 9.
hints: At the intersection, both equations have the same y-value — set them equal.

items.q: Find the intersection of 2x + y = 8 and y = x - 1.
hints: Substitute the expression for y into the other equation.

items.q: Find the equation of the line parallel to y = 3x - 2 through (0,5).
hints: Parallel lines have the same gradient; (0,5) is the y-intercept.

items.q: Are y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x - 9 parallel?
hints: Compare the gradients (the number in front of x) of the two lines.

items.q: Find k if y = kx + 4 is parallel to y = -1/2 x + 1.
hints: The gradient of y = -1/2 x + 1 is -1/2, so k must match it.

items.q: Find the equation of the line parallel to y = -4x + 7 through (1,2).
hints: Parallel lines share the gradient; substitute the point to find c.

items.q: Are y = 5x - 1 and y = 5x + 8 parallel?
hints: Compare the gradients (the number in front of x) of the two lines.

items.q: Find the equation of the line parallel to y = x - 3 through (0,6).
hints: Parallel lines have the same gradient; (0,6) is the y-intercept.

items.q: Find the gradient perpendicular to 2.
hints: Perpendicular gradients multiply to give -1 — take the negative reciprocal.

items.q: Find the equation of the line perpendicular to y = 3x + 1 through the origin.
hints: Take the negative reciprocal of the gradient, then use the given point.
Negative reciprocal of 3 is -1/3; through the origin means c = 0.

items.q: Are y = 1/2 x + 4 and y = -2x + 1 perpendicular?
hints: Multiply the two gradients — perpendicular lines give -1.

items.q: Find the gradient perpendicular to -4.
hints: Perpendicular gradients multiply to give -1 — take the negative reciprocal.

items.q: Find the equation of the line perpendicular to y = x + 2 through (0,5).
hints: Take the negative reciprocal of the gradient, then use the given point.
Negative reciprocal of 1 is -1; (0,5) is the y-intercept.

items.q: Are y = 3x - 2 and y = -1/3 x + 7 perpendicular?
hints: Multiply the two gradients — perpendicular lines give -1.
